  "issueKey": "EVAL-05",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Support console deletion action", "Main database account record", "Data warehouse", "Application logs", "Backups"],
    "dataStores": ["Main database", "Data warehouse", "Logs", "Backups"],

  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Deleted customers' personal data stays readable in the warehouse, logs and backups",
      "scenario": "A customer asks for deletion and the account is only flagged in the main database. Anyone with warehouse, log or backup access (analysts, support staff, an attacker who obtains one of those stores) can still read the full personal records of people who believed their data was erased. There is no propagation of the deletion and no retention limit, so the copies persist indefinitely.",
      "component": "Data warehouse, logs and backups",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Copies in the warehouse, logs and backups are left as is." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-212", "CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "When someone asks to be deleted, only the main copy is marked deleted; their details stay in reporting data, logs and backups.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Propagate deletion to all copies of customer data",
        "given": "a customer's account has been marked as deleted",
        "when": "the deletion is processed",
        "then": "personal data is erased or irreversibly anonymised in the warehouse and logs, and backups are covered by a documented retention window after which the record cannot be restored"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Anyone impersonating a customer can get that customer's account deleted",
      "scenario": "The design says customers can request account deletion and support marks the account as deleted, but no verification of the requester is described. An attacker who knows a customer's email or basic details can contact support, pose as that customer and have the account marked deleted, denying the real owner access and destroying their data.",
      "component": "Deletion request intake (support)",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers can request account deletion. Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-287", "CWE-640"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nothing proves the person asking for deletion owns the account, so someone else could have your account wiped.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Verify the requester owns the account before deletion",
        "given": "a deletion request for an account",
        "when": "support acts on the request",
        "then": "the request is confirmed through an authenticated channel owned by the account holder (for example a signed-in request or a confirmation link to the registered email) and unverified requests are rejected"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Any support agent can delete any account with no authorisation check or limit",
      "scenario": "Deletion is performed by support directly against the main database. No role restriction, approval step or volume limit is described, so a malicious or compromised support account can mark large numbers of customer accounts as deleted, taking customers offline and causing a mass outage of service for them.",
      "component": "Support deletion action on main database",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-285", "CWE-269"],
      "plainLanguage": "Any support agent can flag any account as deleted, and could do it to lots of accounts at once.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict and bound the deletion capability",
        "given": "a support user invoking account deletion",
        "when": "the deletion action is called",
        "then": "the server checks the user holds an explicit deletion role, enforces a per-agent volume threshold with alerting above it, and requires a second approval for bulk deletions"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No record of who requested or performed a deletion",
      "scenario": "The design describes support marking the account as deleted with no record of the request origin, the agent who acted or the time. If a customer disputes a deletion, or an insider deletes accounts maliciously, there is no way to show who did it or to prove the request was genuine — which also undermines the compliance evidence the deletion process exists to provide.",
      "component": "Deletion workflow",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers can request account deletion. Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nobody can tell later who asked for a deletion or which agent carried it out.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Record an immutable deletion trail",
        "given": "an account deletion is carried out",
        "when": "the record is marked deleted",
        "then": "the system stores the verified requester, the acting agent, the timestamp and the scope of erasure in an append-only store that support users cannot edit, and retains it after the account data is erased"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "A deleted-flag account can be silently restored or still accepted as active",
      "scenario": "Because deletion is only a flag on the main database row, the account, its credentials and its warehouse copies still exist. An insider with database or support access can clear the flag to reactivate the account and all its data, and any service or job that reads the record without checking the flag will keep treating the customer as active — for example continuing to process or email them after they asked to be deleted.",
      "component": "Main database account record",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-noop"],
      "plainLanguage": "Deletion is just a tick box, so the account can be switched back on and other systems may still treat it as live.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Make soft deletion enforced and non-reversible by support",
        "given": "an account flagged as deleted",
        "when": "any service authenticates, reads or processes that account",
        "then": "the request is refused, credentials and sessions are invalidated, and clearing the deleted flag is not possible through support tooling"
      }
    }
  ]
